items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No files were kept. All the work ran as throwaway `python3 -c` one-liners, and no decrypt or extract script was left in /app, so there is no persistent code to judge.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: No code change was kept: the decrypt and extract steps were inline shell one-liners. That falls short of the project's 're-runnable decrypt script' convention, but there is no code to judge on structure.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No code was kept. Only ad-hoc inline commands ran, and the XOR key 0x42 was used in them as a bare literal.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: Decoded the header after XOR to get magic 0x377f0682 and page size 4096. Checked the salts and commit fields of all 4 frames, let SQLite replay the WAL in a temp copy, and confirmed with count=11 and `PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok. How the key was chosen isn't shown, but the evidence supports it.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: Made `cp main.db main.db.bak && cp main.db-wal main.db-wal.bak` before opening read-write. That open at step 5 did delete the encrypted WAL, so the backup was what saved it. But the agent later ran `rm main.db.bak main.db-wal.bak`, so the original evidence is gone at the end.
